architecture.mechanism: Real-time pressure parameter monitoring with computerized analysis to identify occlusion events immediately upon occurrence.
architecture.intervention: Integrate a low-cost piezoresistive pressure sensor into the downstream tubing segment of the existing pump, connected to a microcontroller that samples pressure data at high frequency and triggers an alarm when the rate of pressure rise exceeds a predefined threshold indicative of occlusion.
architecture.expected_effect: Reduction in occlusion detection latency from minutes to seconds, preventing excessive pressure buildup and subsequent patient harm while meeting low-cost retrofit constraints through discrete component addition.
architecture.falsification_test: Operate the retrofitted pump in a test bench with a calibrated flow restrictor simulating an occlusion; verify that the system alarms within 5 seconds of occlusion onset across varying flow rates and fails to alarm during normal operation with transient pressure spikes.
